content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp historical spikes (e.g., 76+).
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: forecasts drift downward too quickly after peaks, underestimating subsequent declines.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–3 days in the early part of the horizon, then converge.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the latter half of the forecast window, especially after 20–25 days.
- Overconfidence in short-term spikes leads to overestimation of volatility and price persistence.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after major spikes (e.g., 76.20 → 68.33).
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to reflect sharp, non-linear corrections or sudden drops.
- Model exhibits “anchoring” bias: early forecast values anchor around recent highs, ignoring prior low points.
- Forecasts often underestimate the depth of corrections following spikes, especially in the 20–30 day range.
